question: During a festival sale, an air-conditioner is sold at Rs. 19,750 at a discount of 21%. What is its marked price (in Rs.)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price** be 100%.

**Discount** = 21% → **Selling Price** = 100% − 21% = 79%.

Given 79% = 19750.

100% = (19750 ÷ 79) × 100 = 250 × 100 = 25000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price** (SP) of the **air-conditioner** = ₹19,750

**Discount** percentage = 21%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 − Discount%]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5723ddf28e74df7a34aa0a68559235abc74a7f2c685b36a2d164188dac2e439.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Marked Price** = [19750 × 100] ÷ [100 − 21]

⇒ **Marked Price** = [19750 × 100] ÷ 79

⇒ **Marked Price** = 250 × 100

⇒ **Marked Price** = 25000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price listed on the product by the manufacturer or retailer before any reduction is applied.

Discount Relation

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless stated otherwise. Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, effective discount = [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.
